original_question: Do analytic actions of surface groups on R2 satisfy the Milnor–Wood inequality?
target_in_paper: Section 3.6, Question 3.17 (Calegari): "Do analytic actions of surface groups on R^2 satisfy the Milnor–Wood inequality?"
correct_elements: Your draft already matches the paper almost verbatim: it picks out the exact open problem, keeps the analyticity hypothesis, the acting class of groups (surface groups), the ambient space R^2, and the Milnor–Wood focus. ([conferences.cirm-math.fr](https://conferences.cirm-math.fr/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/Problem_list_3082.pdf))
missing_details: Specify that the action should be by orientation-preserving real-analytic diffeomorphisms of R^2, i.e. a homomorphism ρ: π1(Σ) → Diff^ω_+(R^2).
Specify what "surface group" means in this stand-alone formulation: π1(Σ) for a closed oriented surface Σ; do not broaden to punctured-surface groups.
Specify which Euler class is meant for planar actions: the pullback under ρ of the Euler class e in H^2(Homeo_0(R^2); Z) discussed in Section 3.6.
Spell out "satisfy the Milnor–Wood inequality" as the numerical bound |⟨ρ^*e,[Σ]⟩| ≤ |χ(Σ)|.
Make the quantifier explicit: the question asks whether every such analytic action satisfies that bound.
Do not add extra assumptions such as volume preservation or faithfulness; the paper treats volume preservation as a separate neighboring question (Question 3.18).
refined_question: Let Σ be a closed oriented surface, and let ρ: π1(Σ) → Diff^ω_+(R^2) be an orientation-preserving real-analytic action. If e ∈ H^2(Homeo_0(R^2); Z) denotes the Euler class for planar actions, must the Euler number of ρ, namely ⟨ρ^*e,[Σ]⟩, always satisfy the classical Milnor–Wood bound |⟨ρ^*e,[Σ]⟩| ≤ |χ(Σ)|?
justification: This is exactly Question 3.17 in Section 3.6. The surrounding paragraph gives the intended scope: unrestricted surface-group actions on R^2 do not satisfy Milnor–Wood because the Euler class in H^2(Homeo_0(R^2)) is unbounded, and the paper isolates analyticity as the remaining regularity condition of interest; the volume-preserving version is posed separately as Question 3.18. To make the draft self-contained without broadening it, I only unpacked the Euler-class language from Section 3.5 and the paper’s explicit surface/Milnor–Wood notation from Section 3.7. ([conferences.cirm-math.fr](https://conferences.cirm-math.fr/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/Problem_list_3082.pdf))
